topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Path of Fastest Descent
target_audience: High school physics students and early undergraduate STEM students

sections.title: The Great Race: Intuition vs. Reality
lecture_lines: Which path is the fastest between two points?
Is it the straightest or the steepest path?
Let's compare a straight line and a curve.
Intuitively, the straightest path seems the fastest.
But physics often defies our simple intuition.
animations: Show point A (0, 3) and point B (5, 0) with white labels (#FFFFFF).
Draw three paths: Straight (#FFFFFF), Circular Arc (#FFD700), Steep Curve (#00BFFF).
Place three marbles [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marbles.svg] (White, Gold, Blue) at point A.
Animate marbles [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marbles.svg] sliding; the Blue marble on the steep curve reaches B first.
Highlight the Blue path and label it 'Fastest Path' in blue (#00BFFF).

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Speed and Energy
lecture_lines: Gravity converts potential energy into kinetic energy.
Vertical drop determines the final speed reached.
Total time depends on speed and distance traveled.
animations: Display the energy formula 'mgh = 1/2 mv^2' at the top center in white (#FFFFFF).
Show a marble [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marble.svg] falling; a green bar (#00FF00) labeled 'Speed' grows as height 'h' decreases.
Show the time integral 't = integral(ds/v)' and highlight 'v' in green (#00FF00) and 'ds' in yellow (#FFD700).

sections.title: The Paradox of the Straight Line
lecture_lines: A straight line is the shortest distance.
However, speed is low at the beginning.
A steep curve builds speed much faster.
Higher speed covers more distance in less time.
Speed beats distance in this race.
animations: Draw a straight line (#FFFFFF) and a steep-drop curve (#00BFFF) between two points, with a bicycle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bicycle.svg] starting at the beginning of each path.
Show velocity vectors along both; the curve gets larger vectors (faster speed) much earlier.
Draw a graph showing Velocity vs Time; the curve's line (#00BFFF) is higher than the straight line's (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Fermat’s Principle and the Light Analogy
lecture_lines: Light always follows the path of least time.
It refracts when passing through different media.
Gravity acts like a medium with changing speed.
animations: Show horizontal color bands representing layers where speed increases downward.
Trace a light beam bending at each interface according to Snell's Law.
Increase the number of layers until the path becomes a smooth, continuous curve.
Label the resulting curve 'Path of Least Time' in gold (#FFD700).
Overlay a marble [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marble.svg] sliding along this light-path curve to show the analogy.

sections.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
lecture_lines: The fastest path is called the cycloid.
It is the path of a rolling wheel.
This curve balances acceleration and distance perfectly.
Johann Bernoulli challenged the world with this problem.
The solution revealed a new branch of calculus.
animations: Show a wheel [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wheel.svg] rolling along the top horizontal axis.
Mark a point on the wheel's [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wheel.svg] rim with a bright red dot (#FF0000).
Animate the wheel [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wheel.svg] rolling; the red dot traces an orange path (#FFA500).
Label the orange path 'Cycloid' and scale it to fit points A and B.
Flash the text 'Brachistochrone' in orange (#FFA500) over the curve.

sections.title: The Tautochrone Property (Bonus Insight)
lecture_lines: This curve has another amazing secret property.
Objects released from any point finish together.
This is the "equal time" or tautochrone property.
animations: Draw a large pink cycloid curve (#FF69B4).
Place three marbles [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marbles.svg] at different heights on the left side of the curve.
Release the marbles [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marbles.svg]; show them sliding and converging at the bottom at the same time.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Optimization requires balancing speed and distance.
Cycloids appear in roller coasters and nature.
The fastest path isn't always the straightest one.
animations: Show a split screen with a roller coaster [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rollercoaster.svg] (#00BFFF) and a falcon (#FFD700).
Trace a cycloid curve over both the coaster drop and the falcon's dive path.
Display 'Optimization = Balance of Distance and Speed' in white (#FFFFFF) at the center.
